title: PR Kerfuffle Triage Log — heuristics, action buckets, micro-refactors
content:
Context:
Quick personal log for handling PR-induced incidents (the ones that blow up in CI, cause latency regressions, or introduce flaky behavior). Purpose: capture lightweight heuristics I reach for, short-term remediation actions, and a tiny backlog of follow-ups so we don't leave messes behind.

High-level triage flow (1–5, take fastest safe path):
1) Stop the bleeding: if there's a customer-facing outage or CI gate failing widely, revert (fast) or hotfix (if revert is risky).
2) Gather minimal signals: failing tests, stack traces, perf regression numbers (p50/p95 token/sec), sample request traces, recent deploys/rollouts.
3) Decide action bucket: revert | hotfix | mitigate | monitor-only | patch+followup.
4) Execute with owner and rollback criteria declared in the PR comment.
5) Post-incident: short writeup, assign follow-up tickets, add one-line root-cause to PR for historical context.

Decision heuristics (mental checklist):
- Does the PR change any ABI/endpoints, or schema? If yes -> high risk, prefer revert until QA + contract tests pass.
- Did latency p95 increase > 20% in the last deploy? Treat as performance regression and consider immediate rollback for customer-impacting routes.
- Are failing tests deterministic and limited to a module? If yes -> quick fix in a small PR; if widespread -> revert.
- Does the failure expose data integrity or security issues? Stop everything, escalate to oncall lead and security.
- If flake rate increased < 5% and failures are non-critical tests, prefer monitor + follow-up if no customer impact.

Action buckets (short examples):
- Revert (fast): create revert PR, notify release-channel, mark revert reason in title, add follow-up ticket linking to original PR.
- Hotfix (surgical): change guarded code path, add feature-flag toggle, add quick defensive check (null handling, timeout), deploy to canary then prod.
- Mitigation: reduce load (rate-limit), disable an expensive background job, revert a config change.
- Monitor-only: increase sampling and observability for 24–72h, watch top-10 traces and error rates, defer code changes.
- Patch + Follow-up: land minimal fix, open tickets for deeper cleanup/refactor, add unit/integration tests, plan canary.

Annotated quick checklist to paste in PR comment when triaging (short):
- Symptoms observed (one line)
- Failing CI jobs/tests (list)
- Perf delta (p50/p95 tokens/sec) and sample queries if relevant
- Immediate action taken (revert/hotfix/monitor)
- Rollback criteria (explicit condition to revert hotfix)
- Owner for follow-ups and ETA

Rollback triggers I use (examples):
- >5% customer error-rate increase for 15+ minutes on core routes
- p95 latency regression > 30% vs baseline on production traces
- Data corruption risk (schema mismatch, loss of persisted items)
- Reproducible failing smoke tests for deploy gate

Mini-refactor ideas / cheap safety bets (to reduce future kerfuffles):
- Isolate route adapters: make route-level adapters pure translation layers; keep heavy logic in services with feature-flag toggles. (low friction, high isolation)
- Add idempotency guards on write endpoints and exact-match tests for common dup scenarios.
- Tighten default timeouts for external calls and add clear fallback paths (cache stale serve vs error).
- Small invariant tests for KV-cache behavior (warm vs cold flows) that run in CI smoke stage.
- Add a lightweight perf-smoke that runs a small request batch in CI against the built artifact and asserts p50/p95 not regressing beyond threshold.

Examples of micro-fixes I've applied quickly (notes to self):
- Fix: guard nil pointer in model loader-> hotfix PR, add unit test for nil config.
- Fix: revert accidental debug logging that serialized large tensors-> revert PR, follow up to gate debug logs behind config.
- Fix: narrow locking scope in request pool -> patch + smoke test for throughput.

Follow-up ticket template (one-liner + acceptance):
Title: <short> e.g., "PR 4321: Ensure stable KV-cache invariants and add CI smoke"
Body: root cause summary; proposed actions; owners; acceptance criteria (unit tests added + perf smoke not regressing for 3 runs).

Open questions / things to probe next time:
- Can we automate a lightweight perf-smoke that runs in <90s on CI artifacts? (worth the infra effort)
- Should we add a canary label that blocks rollouts to more than 5% traffic for the first hour for high-risk repos?
- When to prefer revert vs hotfix for feature-flag-protected changes (depends on test coverage + deploy speed).

Quick personal heuristics (mnemonics):
- "Revert fast, explain faster" -> when customer impact clear, prioritize revert + short note.
- "Small guard > big rewrite" -> prefer tiny defensive edits as interim.
- "Document the why" -> if you touch production behavior, write one sentence in PR explaining why change is safe; clears future triage.

Tiny todo list for me (concrete):
- Add perf-smoke prototype to serving-runtime CI (spike, 2d).
- Propose a rollback-template comment in release Slack for oncall to use (copy/paste).
- Grep recent PRs for any unguarded schema changes and add contract tests where missing.

Random quick links I paste often:
- Deploy history: https://internal.redwood/deploys
- Canary playbook: https://confluence.redwood/canary-playbook

End of file. Keep this as a living one-pager; update whenever I hit a new oddball failure pattern.
